registers.safety_notes: Owns a dedicated bespoke_topology transaction driver (jk_topology), not the generic manager. Stage 1 does not alter this driver (roadmap Stage 9/10 scope). Three genuinely separate facts about this field, kept distinct (Stage 3 cell-channel batch, 2026-09-17, and its two same-day user-directed corrections): (1) protocol channel capacity is 32 -- evidenced directly: CellVol/CellWireRes/CellConWireRes all span channel indices 0-31 in both the official PDF (pages 7-10) and the V2 workbook (rows 147-242), a real fact about the register MAP, independent of CellCount's own range. (2) resolve_topology's (batterylifepo4.yaml) own operational acceptance range is now ALSO 1..32 (PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_CAPACITY) -- the resolver no longer enforces a separate, narrower ceiling; a confirmed topology above 16 is accepted on its own merits (mask-exact, in-range voltage plausible, pack-voltage sum matches), the same way 16 always was. This is an acceptance-range change, not a hardware-verification claim: the deployed 16S unit has not been independently tested beyond 16 channels, and the resolver's own confirmation logic (not a hardcoded ceiling) is what continues to gate trust for any topology, including this one. (3) CellCount's OWN documented valid range remains genuinely UNKNOWN -- re-searched both the official PDF and the V2 workbook specifically for a stated range and found neither states one (PDF: no narrative range text near the register, only an unrelated example value "15" in the command-example table; workbook: description column has no range, its "приклад значення" column "16" is this deployed unit's own observed/configured value, not a stated maximum -- see this field's own workbook evidence citation, graded observed_decoded_value, not a range claim). maximum is explicitly null (schema-supported -- 25 other fields in this catalog already use null min/max, all editor_kind:"readonly" like this one) rather than asserting either 16 or 32 as a confirmed protocol maximum for this specific register. No evidence citation was added or removed on this field for either correction (still the same 4 pre-existing citations as before the batch) -- the goal was never to game the verification-status/effective-access derivation cascade either way, only to state plainly what is and is not actually confirmed. Write stays fail-closed regardless of any of the above -- set_cell_count's own set_action (batterylifepo4.yaml) is a hardcoded refusal, independent of this field's derived access.
